newsitem.title: CHINA: Asian airlines eye converted A300 freighters.
newsitem.headline: Asian airlines eye converted A300 freighters.

text.p: Asian airlines are showing interest in converting ageing Airbus A300B4 passenger aircraft into cargo freighters, Airbus Industrie senior marketing analyst, Mike Bausor said.

The carriers realise the potential worth of A300B4 is as a low-cost, medium sized freighter, Bausor said in a recent interview at Airbus headquarters in Toulouse, but declined to name the potential conversion customers.
The B4 conversion package is priced at between $6-7 million carried out by Airbus consortium member Daimler-Benz Aerospace and British Aerospace PLc, Bausor added.

Airbus believes there is a now a rising demand for the "mid-sized"' freighter offering around 45 tonnes capacity over 2,000 nautical miles. The B4 conversion is seen as a cheaper option for airlines instead of buying a new, Airbus A300-600 freighter, he said.
Yesterday Philippine Airlines said it is seeking board approval to convert two of its older generation Airbus A300B4 aircraft into domestic and regional freighters.

Other leading Asian airlines which operate A300s include China Airlines, Garuda Indonesia, Thai Airways and Korean Air Ltd. More than 250 early generation Airbus A300s are still flying, many of them candidates for conversion as they reach 15-20 years old and are replaced by more efficient and passenger friendly models such as the A330.

"Airlines now think that they have a much more valuable product on their hands than they did a couple of years ago. The B4 has now reached maturity and no longer has appeal as a passenger aircraft and the value of the aircraft is now low enough to make it very attractive to be converted into a freighter. We are targetting Asia-based individual airlines and interest is being shown," he said.

Airbus' cargo traffic forecasts up to 2015 for intra- Asian and Pacific regions show the highest average growth rates at 9.3 and 9.2 per cent per annum repectively. - Reuters Air Cargo Service Tel+ 44 171 542 7706 Fax +5017 - www.racs.com
